chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan the third (peace be upon him) asking him about vision and what people say about it. He wrote back (peace be upon him): 'Vision is not valid unless there is air between the seer and the seen that the eye can penetrate. When the air is cut off and the presence of light between the seer and the seen is lacking, vision is not valid and there is confusion in that, because when the seer equals the seen in the cause necessitated between them for vision, confusion becomes obligatory, and there is analogy in that, because causes must be connected to their effects.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for valid vision according to Imam al-Naqi in al-Tawhid?
ai.summary: Imam al-Naqi (AS) clarifies that divine vision is not absolute but contingent upon the presence of a visual medium (air) and light, thereby refuting the anthropomorphists who claim God can be seen with physical eyes. By establishing that the seer and the seen must share similar causal conditions for vision to occur, he argues that if God were visible, He would be subject to the limitations of corporeal entities, leading to inevitable confusion and analogy (tashbih). This nuanced view supports the Shia theological stance that while vision is possible, it is not the unrestricted, physical sight attributed to created beings.
